transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-10-12 15:00 UTC | Duration 42m | Attendees: Jordan Lee, Priya Nair, Luis Moreno (Redwood); Maya Patel, Evan Ross, Samir Khan, Alicia Gomez (Hera)

Summary: short postmortem review of the 2026-09-27 production incident where Hera saw elevated tail latency and intermittent 503s on hosted inference. Discussed RCA (KV cache eviction + burst pattern + autoscaler edge), mitigations (prefix caching, autoscale tuning, fallback to smaller model), compliance notes (KMS keys, audit logs), and agreed next steps: run targeted benchmarks in Dedicated staging, share logs and request traces, update incident playbook and SLA language.

Topics: Root cause, immediate mitigations, long-term reliability changes, benchmarking plan, security/compliance concerns, next steps/action items

--- Transcript body ---
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We wanted to run through the postmortem for the 9/27 incident and make sure the follow-up work is clearly owned. I sent the draft postmortem link earlier, but I'll drop it again in the chat after the call.
[00:18] Maya Patel: thanks Jordan. Saw the doc, skimmed — big concern for us is the customer-facing SLAs; marketing freaked out when some of our users hit errors. We need concrete remediation and timelines.
[00:30] Evan Ross: yeah the error spikes correlated with a traffic burst from a batch of inference jobs. We saw KV cache thrashing at the same time, our p99 jumped from ~120ms to 2.1s and then 503s.
[00:47] Priya Nair: quick context from Redwood side: during the burst the serving runtime's cache eviction policy ended up evicting prefixes needed by a lot of concurrent sessions. The autoscaler also triggered scale-up but there's a short window where requests hit newly spawned workers without warmed KV. That combination is what produced the tail latency and the transient 503s.
[01:10] Samir Khan: is that the KV-cache you mentioned in the docs? we call this hot-prefix problem on our end. There's also a note that the requests had unusually long prompt lengths which exacerbated memory pressure.
[01:28] Priya Nair: yes, it's the same. Also worth flagging that the model variant in hosted was the large-quantized model; in that workload we see bigger kv footprint.
[01:40] Maya Patel: can you remind me why the autoscaler allowed the sudden burst to cause 503s? shouldn't fallback to a smaller model or queued requests have prevented failures?
[01:52] Jordan Lee: good question. Right now our policy is to favor low-latency autoscale with hard capacity limits; when warm workers are exhausted we spin new ones, but the scheduler doesn't automatically fall back to model variants unless configured at the route level. We had route defaults for Hera but not an aggressive fallback policy.
[02:10] Alicia Gomez: from security/compliance — did the incident expose any customer data? we need the audit log and KMS access checks.
[02:20] Luis Moreno: quick answer: no evidence of data exfiltration; logs show transient errors and retries. We kept request payloads in transient memory and nothing was written to durable storage. We'll provide audit logs and an event timeline.
[02:36] Evan Ross: one confusing thing — some of the logs reference request IDs that don't match our internal tracing because the agent strips or maps IDs, can you map X-Request-ID to Redwood request IDs?
[02:47] Priya Nair: absolutely. We'll include a mapping table — please send the top 10 X-Request-IDs you have and we'll map them.
[02:55] Maya Patel: ok we'll pull those. On remediation: are there short-term mitigations we can put in place while infra changes are made?
[03:04] Priya Nair: short term we recommend three actions: 1) enable prefix caching for the most common prompts (reduces KV load), 2) configure a soft fallback to a smaller model variant for the route when queue depth exceeds threshold, 3) tune autoscaler cooldowns to reduce thrash. These are relatively quick config changes.
[03:24] Jordan Lee: and from product ops we can push a temporary rate limit on durations to blunt the burst — that's less ideal but available.
[03:32] Samir Khan: will prefix caching change output quality? some of our prompts rely on exact context.
[03:39] Priya Nair: it can, if misconfigured. We'll share a suggested prompt whitelist and how to do selective caching so you can avoid quality regressions.
[03:50] Maya Patel: perfect, please share the whitelist.
[03:54] Evan Ross: longer-term — what are your plans for making Dedicated or Private a more robust option? We may want to move critical workflows to Dedicated if Hosted can't meet our SLOs.
[04:06] Luis Moreno: Dedicated offers predictable throughput and reserved capacity; we can also pre-warm KV cache on Dedicated nodes because you control the model pinning and pool size. The tradeoff is cost and the setup lead time.
[04:19] Maya Patel: if we do a Dedicated pilot, can you run a benchmark with our real traffic patterns? that's what we really need to validate.
[04:26] Jordan Lee: yes — next step is to schedule a 1-hour benchmark in Dedicated staging with your payload. Luis will own scheduling. We'll collect p50/p90/p99 and token costs.
[04:37] Alicia Gomez: for Private/VPC we need to confirm KMS/HSM key management — specifically if logs or telemetry are sent to Redwood control plane or kept customer-side.
[04:48] Luis Moreno: control plane telemetry is opt-in for Private; for Dedicated we have options. We'll document what is sent, and provide config for customer-managed KMS, plus SOC2 artifacts.
[04:58] Maya Patel: please send SOC2 and the KMS integration doc.
[05:03] Jordan Lee: will do. Also note — we spotted an internal edge-case where the autoscaler didn't rehydrate caches fast enough when workers came up due to a kernel selection path that avoids eager KV-prefetch to save memory. Priya is going to run a regression to quantify the hit.
[05:18] Priya Nair: yes I'm already on it, I'll run a KV-prefetch vs no-prefetch microbenchmark and share a spreadsheet. Early numbers show ~35-40% p99 reduction when prefetch is enabled for that workload, but it increases memory usage.
[05:33] Samir Khan: memory bump is ok if performance is stable — we'll need numbers.
[05:37] Priya Nair: understood.
[05:40] Evan Ross: one more ask — can Redwood add a toggle in console to enable the model fallback policy per-route? currently it's a hidden config we don't have direct access to.
[05:50] Jordan Lee: good product ask — we'll raise a feature request, but I can also flip it on for your routes manually in the short term.
[05:58] Maya Patel: thanks. On timelines, Hera needs to close the loop with their execs next week; concise artifacts would help.
[06:05] Jordan Lee: action items recap: send updated postmortem with timeline and RCA (Jordan), Priya runs KV tests and shares perf spreadsheet (Priya), Hera to share X-Request-IDs and logs (Maya/Evan), Luis schedules Dedicated benchmark (Luis), Alicia lists compliance docs for KMS (Alicia). We'll reconvene after benchmark.
[06:26] Luis Moreno: I'm going to propose an initial autoscaler config we think will reduce thrash and include a canary policy to roll it slowly.
[06:33] Samir Khan: can we do a quick test in staging with 10x the traffic to validate the new autoscaler?
[06:39] Priya Nair: yes, staging test is exactly what we'll run as part of the benchmark. We'll record metrics and provide a dashboard link.
[06:46] Jordan Lee: ok, any final questions?
[06:49] Alicia Gomez: one small question — in the postmortem you noted 'no PII left on disk' but our legal wants assurance on temp logs — can you spell out retention and scrub steps?
[06:58] Luis Moreno: yes, we'll include retention windows and scrub steps in the doc. For Hosted we keep ephemeral request data for 72 hours by default, and transit copies are not persisted. We'll include a configuration option for shorter retention.
[07:12] Maya Patel: thanks, that's helpful.
[07:15] Jordan Lee: thanks everyone — we'll follow up via the doc and schedule the benchmark. I'll drop the postmortem link in the calendar note and send the action item list.
[07:24] Meeting end.

References / artifacts: draft postmortem doc (link sent via calendar), KV-prefetch microbenchmark spreadsheet (to be shared), Dedicated staging benchmark plan (will be created by Luis), SOC2 and KMS integration docs (Redwood Security pack)

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker mislabels and small transcription errors present (e.g., "kv cache" sometimes transcribed as "k v cash")
